title: Disk full!
summary: 3 a.m., "No space left on device". Measure with df and du, find the monster file, compress and truncate logs safely, and catch the space thief that df sees but ls can't.

nodes.bourbon: the order server; its data disk is /srv/data (64 MB)

tasks.title: How bad is it?
tasks.text: How full is the filesystem mounted at `/srv/data`? Submit the **Use%** number that `df` reports (just the number, without `%`).
hints: `df -h` lists every mounted filesystem with its size, used, available and Use%. `-h` means human units (M, G).
`df -h /srv/data` shows just the one you care about.

tasks.title: Where did it all go?
tasks.text: `df` says *how full*, `du` says *what is using it*. Which folder directly inside `/srv/data` takes up the most space? Submit its name.
hints: `du -sh /srv/data/*` prints a total for each item in `/srv/data` (`-s` summary, `-h` human units).
Sort it, biggest last: `du -sh /srv/data/* | sort -h`. Hidden folders are included in each folder's total.

answer_cmd.cmd: du -s /srv/data/* | sort -n | tail -1 | awk '{print $2}' | xargs basename

tasks.title: Evict the monster
tasks.text: Somewhere in that folder is a single file of almost 30 MB that has no business on an order server. Find it and delete it.

checks.fail_msg: There is still a file over 20 MB under /srv/data.
Today's orders or the live log went missing. Restart the lab: only the monster had to go.

hints: Keep drilling down with `du -sh <folder>/*`, or ask `find` straight away: `find /srv/data -type f -size +20M`.
Plain `ls` hides folders whose names start with a dot; `ls -la` shows them. Found it? `rm <path>`.

tasks.title: Squash the old logs
tasks.text: `/srv/data/logs` holds yesterday's rotated logs `app.log.1`, `app.log.2` and `app.log.3`. We must keep them, but they don't need to be readable at full size. **Compress** each with gzip, so they become `app.log.1.gz` and so on.

checks.fail_msg: app.log.1.gz, app.log.2.gz and app.log.3.gz don't all exist yet.
The uncompressed copies are still there (gzip replaces the file unless you ask it to keep it).

hints: `gzip file` replaces `file` with a much smaller `file.gz`. Log text squashes well, often to a tenth.
One command for all three: `gzip /srv/data/logs/app.log.[1-3]`. Read them later with `zcat` or `zgrep`, no need to unpack.

tasks.title: Shrink the live log (carefully)
tasks.text: `app.log` is 14 MB and `biscuit-api` is **still writing to it**. Empty it so it starts again from zero, while keeping `biscuit-api` running and still logging into `/srv/data/logs/app.log`.

checks.fail_msg: biscuit-api is not running any more! Restart the lab and try again without stopping it.
/srv/data/logs/app.log is missing or still bigger than 1 MB.
biscuit-api is writing into a deleted file, not into /srv/data/logs/app.log (did the file get removed and recreated?).

hints: Deleting a file that a program has open does **not** free the space: the program keeps writing into the now-invisible file, and the new `app.log` you create stays empty.
Empty it in place instead: `truncate -s 0 /srv/data/logs/app.log`, or the classic `: > /srv/data/logs/app.log`. Same file, now zero bytes.

tasks.title: The invisible space thief
tasks.text: Check `df -h /srv/data` again. Add up what `du -sh /srv/data` sees: about 10 MB are missing! Gary deleted a 10 MB debug log, but some process is still holding it open. Find the process and free that space.

checks.fail_msg: A process still holds a deleted file under /srv/data open.

hints: Every open file of every process is listed in `/proc/<PID>/fd/` as a link. A deleted one ends in `(deleted)`. Usually you'd use `lsof +L1`, but this server doesn't have lsof.
`ls -l /proc/[0-9]*/fd 2>/dev/null | grep deleted` shows the link. To see **which** process: `find /proc/[0-9]*/fd -lname '*(deleted)' 2>/dev/null` (the number after /proc/ is the PID).
Restart or kill that process (`ps -p <PID> -o args` tells you who it is), or, if it must stay up, truncate the file through its fd: `: > /proc/<PID>/fd/<N>`.
